headline: Nvidia beat and guided to $130 billion, so chip futures rose this morning, but stocks fell 1% Tuesday on software and health insurer selling; ANET and ADI held their buy points, TMO's swing setup ended, and no put passes the screen.
summary: Prices on the dashboard are Tuesday Nov 17 closes and match Massive. The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53, its lowest close since July, the Dow 1.64% and the Nasdaq 100 0.72% (Barchart); SPY closed 732.44. Software led the drop (Salesforce down more than 9%), and health insurers fell after CMS proposed wider Medicare Advantage audits (UNH -5.42%). After the close Nvidia reported $115.84 billion of revenue, up 103%, and guided to $130 billion against about $125 billion expected; it rose about 2.7% before the open, and Nasdaq futures were up about 0.9% at 6:47am ET (Reuters). The 10 year sat at 5.10% and gold fell 2.5% to $3,768 (Wall Street Breakfast). Plan: let today's close, not the premarket, decide AI entries; WM is the new swing setup; TMO's setup is void after a close under its stop; still no put idea.

regime.why: Tuesday was risk off: stocks fell, the VIX rose to 25.46 and futures still price a quarter point December hike with near 100% odds (Barchart). This morning Nvidia's outlook lifted chip futures, but gold and bitcoin kept falling and the Fed minutes come at 2pm ET. One good report does not undo a week of selling; wait for the close.

signals.title: Nvidia beat and raised: $115.8 billion of sales, a $130 billion guide, and no China in the number
signals.since_yesterday: The report is out: revenue and the guide beat, the board ruled out bringing back the founder, and the stock rose about 2.7% before the open.
signals.what_happened: Nvidia's quarterly revenue rose 103.2% to $115.84 billion; data center revenue rose 110% to $107.60 billion; adjusted EPS was $2.68 (Investing.com). It guided this quarter to $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, against $125.25 billion expected (LSEG via Reuters). Interim CEO Colette Kress said it sold $2.4 billion of licensed Hopper chips to China last quarter, will ship no more, and the guide includes none. The new chair said the board does not plan to reinstate Jensen Huang; Huang and the general counsel are due before Congress early next month (Investing.com). Before the open NVDA was up about 2.7%; AMD +1.9%, AVGO +2.2%, MU +2.7%, MRVL +3.2%, CoreWeave +4.4% and Nebius +6.4% (Reuters). Tuesday's closes (Massive): NVDA 155.46 (-0.44%), ANET 186.42 (-0.32%), ADI 383.67 (+0.13%; its intraday low 377.91 was under its 382.16 point, but it closed over it), TSM 359.69 (-3.68%).
signals.so_what: Who pays: the cloud companies and model labs, whose spending still grows faster than any supplier can build. Who gets paid: Nvidia first, then memory, networking and the neoclouds that rent its chips. What changed: demand risk fell, policy risk did not. China is now zero in the guide, so the Thursday license rule hits customers outside China, not Nvidia's China line. What would make this wrong: a premarket pop that fades by the close, as happened to several AI names this month; TSM closed under its post drop box on 2.12x volume Tuesday, a confirmed break down.
signals.for_you: Long term: ANET (186.42, point 181.27) and ADI (383.67, point 382.16) held their points into the report. ADI is still on the long term scan buy list; ANET dropped to 'Wait' because sellers outweigh buyers on volume. ADI reports Nov 24 (unconfirmed), so a first piece now carries a report in four days. Puts: none on AI names; ADI's report falls inside any December expiry. Swing: no AI setups are live; TSM is a confirmed break down, so no puts there.

signals.title: Chip license rule: the administration is going ahead, but the start date is still not confirmed
signals.since_yesterday: Nvidia's guide now assumes no China data center sales, and the administration is moving ahead with the rule as Trump meets Xi and Putin Thursday.
signals.what_happened: The Commerce rule needs a license to ship advanced chips to any data center that rents large amounts of computing to companies based in China, Macau or other restricted countries; data centers already serving them get 90 days after it takes effect to get a license (StockAnalysis; CNN). Reports said it takes effect when published in the Federal Register; the public copy leaves the dates blank, so Thursday is not confirmed. Wall Street Breakfast reported the administration is moving ahead with it, and UBS's Paul Donovan said China's most disruptive answer might be limits on rare earth exports.
signals.so_what: Second order: the five newly covered countries (Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Brazil) are where many Asian data center builds sit, so server makers and data center landlords there carry the delay, not Nvidia's guide. Third order: a rare earth answer from Beijing would hit magnet users and favor non China supply. The meeting Thursday could soften or harden all of this. Confidence in timing is low.
signals.for_you: No action. Do not sell puts on AI hardware names through Thursday's meeting. MP insiders keep buying (see smart money), but MP is in a downtrend, so it is a watch item, not a buy.

signals.title: Medicare Advantage audits: CMS wants about $9 billion a year back, and insurers fell 2% to 5%
signals.what_happened: CMS proposed rule CMS-6098-P (the 'CRUSH' proposal) on Nov 16. It would audit Medicare Advantage risk adjustment data without a fee for service adjuster and extrapolate findings back to payment year 2018; CMS estimates about $9 billion recovered per payment year. It also makes fraud referrals by plans mandatory and requires providers who bill Medicare Advantage to enroll in Original Medicare. Comments are due Jan 19, 2027 (GuruFocus). A Texas judge vacated the 2023 audit rule in September 2025 after a Humana suit. Tuesday's closes (Massive): UNH 389.68 (-5.42%) on 8.05M shares, ELV 433.93 (-2.77%), CI 294.06 (-2.03%), HUM 443.34, CVS 85.81; Barchart had Humana and CVS down more than 3%.
signals.so_what: Who pays: the plans with the most coded risk scores, UNH first as the largest Medicare Advantage insurer. Who gets paid: the Medicare trust fund. Second order: plans that expect clawbacks tighten prior authorization and cut extras, which reaches clinics, home health and coding vendors. What would make this wrong: the last version lost in court, and a final rule is months away, so this is a slow overhang, not a cliff. Watch the comment record and any legal challenge.
signals.for_you: Puts: none on insurers while this sits open. Swing: UNH closed 389.68, 0.7% over its range low (387.14), which was set Tuesday; a close under it on 8,278,000+ shares would confirm a break (that alert was not set today, see actions). CI closed 294.06, 0.8% over its range low 291.57 (alert live) and 2.0% over its long term point 288.26; it stays 'Wait' because sellers outweigh buyers. ELV fell out of its range up watch list, so its alert was deleted.

signals.title: Tuesday's tape: S&P 500 at its lowest close since July, software down hard, Fed still set to hike
signals.what_happened: The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53, the Dow 1.64% to 50,759.42 and the Nasdaq 100 0.72% (Barchart). Software led: Salesforce fell more than 9%, Intuit more than 7%, ServiceNow, Atlassian and Workday more than 6% (Barchart). Nike fell 6.30% after its investor day pointed to a hard next year, and Home Depot 2.45% on its outlook. Data: the NAHB builder index fell to 25, a 14 year low; import prices outside oil rose 0.8% against 0.5% expected. New York Fed President Williams said more hikes are likely but 'the situation does not call for dramatic action'; St. Louis Fed President Musalem said several hikes may be needed before spring 2027. Futures price a 100% chance of a quarter point hike on Dec 9 (Barchart).
signals.so_what: Money left long duration growth (software) and anything with policy risk (insurers), while rates stayed near 5.1%. A 14 year low in builder sentiment with a hiking Fed says housing stays frozen. The VIX rose to 25.46 even on a smaller drop than Monday, so hedges are getting more expensive, which makes put premiums richer but breakouts less reliable. The Fed minutes at 2pm ET today can move rates either way.
signals.for_you: Swing: smaller size and only closes on 1.5x volume count. Puts: richer premiums do not fix thin options; the bar is the 10 year at 5.10%. Long term: no change to the buy list from this.

cycle.quadrant: Growth rising and inflation rising (overheating), with housing and confidence cracking
cycle.quadrant_why: Import prices outside oil rose 0.8% in October against 0.5% expected, and retail sales outside autos rose 0.6% (Barchart). But the NAHB builder index fell to 25, a 14 year low, and S&P 500 profits are still on track to grow about 31% from a year ago with 84% of companies beating (Barchart).
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening and late. A December quarter point hike is priced at 100%; Musalem sees several hikes before spring 2027 while Williams rules out 'dramatic action' (Barchart). The 10 year holds near 5.10%.
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. Long yields above 5% while the central bank hikes into a 14 year low in housing sentiment leaves little room to cut if growth breaks. Government is now hunting for money inside its own programs, as the $9 billion a year Medicare Advantage audit plan shows.
cycle.big_cycle: External order and technology are the active forces. External order: a chip license rule and a Trump, Xi and Putin meeting in the same week, with rare earths as China's likely answer. Technology: Nvidia's sales doubled in a year, but its leadership is in turmoil.
tailwinds: Nvidia's guide rose about $22 billion in one quarter.
Corporate profits are growing about 31% a year (Barchart).
Long bonds still rally on down days for stocks.
headwinds: A Fed hike priced at 100% for Dec 9.
Policy shocks in two sectors at once: chips and health insurance.

history.when: 1994 to early 1995: the Fed's surprise hiking run
history.what: The Fed raised rates seven times in 13 months, taking the federal funds rate from 3.05% to 6.05%; more than $1 trillion was wiped off the bond market by November 1994.
history.lesson: A hiking Fed can hurt prices even while the economy and profits are fine. In that kind of year, patience beats chasing breakouts.

source.title: Wikipedia: 1994 bond market crisis (the Great Bond Massacre)

cycle.differences: In 1994 inflation was low and the Fed hiked early. Today inflation is already high and long yields are over 5%, so the Fed is hiking late. And today one company's sales can move the whole index, which 1994 did not have.
cycle.for_you: Swing: live setups are WM and MO, both defensive; size small, closes on 1.5x volume only. Puts: nothing passed; the bar is 5.10% a year and most buy list options are too thin. Long term: GD, PFE and ADI are at their points; buy in pieces and mind ADI's Nov 24 report.
